page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.16-256 is an x86_64 architecture virtual server configured with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via two threads per core. Driven by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, this server type delivers dedicated, non-burstable CPU allocation to eliminate noisy-neighbor interference during demanding processing cycles.

The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This elevated memory density positions the shape effectively for memory-heavy configurations. The system does not include integrated local storage, meaning all persistent data and operating filesystem operations depend entirely on network-attached block volumes. There are no graphics acceleration units bundled on this machine, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.16-256 provides a high ratio of RAM relative to CPU cores, reducing the total core count required to host massive working datasets. Because persistent I/O relies entirely on remote block storage, architecture planning must account for network volume throughput. This profile is engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory relational databases, distributed key-value caches, analytical data processing, and large-scale application backends.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.16-256 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 256 GB of system RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor running at 3.9 GHz with simultaneous multithreading, it delivers a generous memory allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. The server carries no local storage drives, requiring external network storage for disk operations, and provides no hardware GPU acceleration. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With high-frequency execution cores paired with substantial memory density, this server provides a balanced profile for systems requiring extensive memory footprints without demanding local NVMe storage arrays. It is designed to handle memory-heavy workloads, including in-memory caching solutions, enterprise databases, and data processing systems.
